  "text": "Tobias Reel came down the church road in the morning because he was the only one who would.\n\nThe tide was where the almanac said it should be. There were gulls. The wind came off the water with its usual bad breath and he was grateful for every bit of it.\n\nThe posts were all there. He counted them twice, from the porch end, and the eleventh stood dry to its foot and did not make a sound.\n\nThe door was shut. He put his thumb to the latch and it gave the way a latch gives when nobody has lifted it in a while. Inside, the front room was cold. The lamp stood on the sill with its chipped base turned to the wall. He touched the glass. There was no warmth in it and no smell of oil, and the wick was white.\n\nHer father's rug lay square to the boards. It was dry.\n\nHe did not look through the window at the sea. He stood with his back to it, as her mother had never done, and found that he could not say what he was waiting for, only that it had stopped mattering what he did.\n\nAfter a while he went out and shut the door and heard the latch take.\n\nOn the path the lantern hung still. He left it. Halfway up, he thought he heard a single knock from the beach, far down, dull, like a knuckle on a table in another room.\n\nHe went on. He did not count.",
